bibliographic.title: Development and validation of an artificial intelligence proof-of-concept tool for risk-based quality assessment of generic medicines: a South African case study
bibliographic.authors: Danks, L.; Semete-Makokotlela, B.; Reynecke, C.; Dijeng, S.; Kgosietsile, B.; van Tonder, J.; van Graan, C.; Hinch, J.; Kruger, A.; Walker, S.; Salek, S.
bibliographic.citation_apa: Danks, L., Semete-Makokotlela, B., Reynecke, C., Dijeng, S., Kgosietsile, B., van Tonder, J., van Graan, C., Hinch, J., Kruger, A., Walker, S., & Salek, S. (2026). Development and validation of an artificial intelligence proof-of-concept tool for risk-based quality assessment of generic medicines: A South African case study. Frontiers in Medicine, 13, 1811333. https://doi.org/10.3389/fmed.2026.1811333

methodology.method_family: proof-of-concept development and GAMP5-based validation case study
methodology.study_design: development and external validation of an AI RBA triage tool across two African NRAs using IQ/OQ/PQ qualification phases
methodology.sample_description: 210 SAHPRA product dossiers for development; external validation across 60 dossiers at SAHPRA and BoMRA with human assessors-in-the-loop
methodology.technology_context: RAG architecture with Meta Llama 3.1, vector embeddings, regulatory knowledge base integrations (EDQM, WHO PQ), Docker deployment, document intelligence pipeline

eligibility.decision_rationale: The study provides empirical evidence on LLM-based RAG deployment, validation, auditability, and governance in a highly regulated medicines context, but the provided text describes dossier triage and document intelligence rather than conversational AI, chatbots, agents, or conversational governance mechanisms.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: High automated relevance score despite zero conversational-AI signals; confirm whether non-conversational RAG regulatory tools should be coded as supporting or excluded under the review's conversational-governance scope.

appraisal.notes: Clear PoC development and GAMP5-aligned validation with quantitative performance metrics and human assessors-in-the-loop; limited provided text on broader limitations and no conversational-governance design.

cerqual.explanation: Methodologically coherent empirical validation of an LLM-RAG regulatory tool with transparent qualification phases, but direct relevance to conversational governance is low because the supplied text does not describe dialogue systems, user interaction governance, or conversational oversight mechanisms.

coding.theme: LLM-RAG governance for regulated document assessment
rq_alignment: audit and validation of AI systems

synthesis.main_claim: LEXI, an AI proof-of-concept using RAG with Llama 3.1, was developed from SAHPRA's RBA quality matrix and externally validated under GAMP5, achieving 91.7% overall predictive accuracy across 60 dossiers at two African NRAs.
synthesis.contribution: Offers an empirical regulated-domain case of LLM-RAG system design, grounding, security-conscious deployment, and formal validation for medicines dossier triage rather than conversational interaction.
synthesis.limitations: Provided text notes LLM limitations with mathematical equations affecting one criterion and indicates need for further validation across broader product types and regulatory environments; conversational governance is not addressed.
synthesis.use_in_review: Include as supporting evidence for operational governance, validation, auditability, and human-in-the-loop oversight of LLM-RAG systems in regulated health/pharma contexts; not central evidence for conversational governance.

evidence.claim: Study uses a specific LLM with RAG in a regulated medicines workflow
evidence.excerpt: The system employed Retrieval- Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture with Meta’s Llama 3.1 large language model

evidence.claim: Empirical validation design with defined sample sizes
evidence.excerpt: using 210 of its product dossiers, and was validated under the Good Automated Manufacturing Practice (GAMP5) framework

evidence.claim: External validation across two NRAs on 60 dossiers with reported accuracy
evidence.excerpt: During external validation across 60 dossiers, LEXI demonstrated 91.7% overall predictive accuracy (55/60; 95% CI: 81.6-97.2%)
with the final tool testing and validation with “human assessors-in-the-loop” to assure the acceptable accuracy of the AI tool

evidence.claim: RAG outputs are grounded in regulatory knowledge base
evidence.excerpt: Upon receiving a query, the system retrieved pertinent context from its indexed knowledge base and used this to guide the LLM’s reasoning, thereby grounding all AI-generated outputs in the provided regulatory texts

evidence.claim: Auditability and regulatory accountability are explicit design goals
evidence.excerpt: maintaining regulatory accountability and supporting validation audits

evidence.claim: Security-centric deployment limits external data transfer
evidence.excerpt: Local hosting of the language model and data processing pipeline prevented the transfer of any confidential regulatory data to external servers or cloud services
the AI use complied with data privacy and governance frameworks

evidence.claim: No conversational system described in supplied text
evidence.excerpt: The RBA AI PoC tool, which was nicknamed LEXI (Linguistic Expert), was developed over the course of 18 months, using the Large Language Model (LLM), Llama 3.1

evidence.claim: Known LLM limitation affecting performance on symbolic content
evidence.excerpt: LLMs, which enable systems to understand, interpret, and generate human language, are not well- suited for directly handling mathematical equations as these are symbolic, not linguistic
